key_claims: Mood subsumes phantasia not by replacement but by 'ontological completion'
Where Aristotle gives us a mechanistic, causal ontology, Heidegger gives us a phenomenological ontology
Phantasia is the 'middle term': the dynamic ontological-psychological space where moods crystallize into emotions and emotions reverberate back into world-disclosure
Attunement to environment is the existential constitution that makes perception meaningful
notes: Contains the chapter's culminating thesis. The 'middle term' formulation (p. 22) is the single most important sentence in both chapters. Contains Tensions #10 (subsumption vs complementarity) and #12 (mechanistic vs phenomenological).
